chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad and ʿAbd Allāh, the two sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Dāwūd al-Ṣarmī, who said:
I saw Abā al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام more than once urinate, then take a small jug and pour water over it immediately.
His statement, 'he pours water over it,' indicates that the amount of water is more than the amount of the remaining urine, because only an amount exceeding that would be poured.

Then he said: Whoever has become junub and wants to perform ghusl, let him not put his hand into the water when it is in a vessel until he washes it three times. If his wudu (ablution) is due to defecation, then let him wash it twice before putting it in, as we have mentioned. And from the occurrence of urination, he washes it once before putting it into the vessel, and likewise from the occurrence of sleep.

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: entered the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.كُوزًا: a small jug or vessel for water

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about washing after urination and cleaning the hand before ghusl or wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام regarding cleansing after urination and gives rulings about washing the hand before placing it into water kept in a vessel. It highlights rules of taharah and precautions related to impurity in acts connected to wudu (ablution) and ghusl.
